[cheerful] New lesson: counting orders by city.

Link several tables, then group the results to calculate.
elements.apres: The sales team wonders which cities order the most.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] The sales team wonders which cities order the most.

It wants to know how many orders were placed in each city.

For this, we get the city of each customer from the customers table,

And the orders to count from the orders table.

But the orders table only has the customer’s ID, not their city.

So we need to combine the two tables to count the orders of each city.
elements.avant: Link several tables, then group the results to calculate.
elements.apres: First try: group the customers table by city, with group by.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] First, inner join links the tables. Then, group by groups the rows.

Thanks to the join, each order gets its customer’s city: 15 rows.

Group by customers dot city gathers the orders of the same city: one group per city.

Finally, count counts the orders in each group: each group becomes a single row.
